name: Saddle Brown
lede: Saddle Brown is a dark, warm leather brown, one of the 140 named colors in the X11 set for websites.

sections.title: A leather brown, set as a web color
sections.body:
Paterson calls SaddleBrown a dark brown from the X11 web set of 140 named colours, hex code #8B4513 [1]. The index lists it among the browns with an asterisk for X11 [2][3]. The books give no earlier history for the name; it reads as the color of saddle leather and is documented only as a standard [1].

Other browns in the index include [[russet]] and [[sandalwood]] [3]. A lighter relative in the same X11 set is [[sandy-brown]] [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, 746 hold this color at 5% of the canvas or more, as photographed [4]. The oldest sample is a narrative scroll from Andhra Pradesh, 1870 [4]. Printed use of *saddle brown* peaked around 1942 [5]. The match counts any painting with this color covering at least a twentieth of the canvas, so it shows where the color appears in photographs of paintings, not that the painters ever called it by this name.
